children: The Aditya Birla Group has taken its first formal step toward entering the aircraft-leasing business, with its newly incorporated GIFT City entity, UHG Holdings IFSC Pvt Ltd, seeking regulatory approval to undertake aircraft leasing activities.

The application, made to the GIFT-Multiservice Special Economic Zone Approval Committee, marks the group’s entry into the rapidly expanding aircraft-finance ecosystem at Gujarat International Finance Tec-City (GIFT City). Three Aditya Birla Group companies—Hindalco Industries, UltraTech Cement, and Grasim Industries —incorporated UHG Holdings on August 20, 2026. The proposed company will undertake aircraft-leasing activities under the regulatory framework of the International Financial Services Centres Authority (IFSCA).

Aircraft leasing is a capital-intensive business in which lessors typically acquire aircraft and lease them to airlines. UHG Holdings will be owned by three Aditya Birla Group companies, with Hindalco holding 50%, UltraTech Cement 41%, and Grasim Industries 9%.

The company has been set up with an initial paid-up capital of ₹10 lakh. However, the incorporation documents indicate that it can fund its operations through shareholder contributions as well as borrowings. The move gives the Aditya Birla Group an entry into a specialised financial business that has been steadily developing in GIFT City, as India seeks to build a domestic hub for aircraft financing and leasing.

Aditya Birla Group’s entry comes as GIFT City’s aircraft-leasing ecosystem attracts some of India’s biggest business and airline groups. The Adani Group has set up aircraft-leasing vehicles in the IFSC, while Tata Group’s Air India and IndiGo have established GIFT City entities to finance and lease aircraft. Akasa Air has also set up an IFSC leasing arm as it expands its fleet. Aditya Birla Group’s entry is notable because, unlike the airline groups, it is entering aircraft leasing as a new business through a consortium of its industrial companies.

The timing also comes as the GIFT City market has grown rapidly. As of June 2026, 37 aircraft-leasing entities were operating from the IFSC, with a combined portfolio of 412 aviation assets, including 237 aircraft, 87 engines and 85 APUs. Financing extended by International Banking Units to aircraft-leasing entities stood at $664.77 million at the end of June 2026, compared with $234.6 million a year earlier. The expansion suggests that aircraft leasing is emerging as a significant business within GIFT City’s financial ecosystem — and UHG Holdings will now look to establish its position in that market.

In May this year, the bussinessline had reported that major Indian airlines, including IndiGo, Air India, Akasa Air and Star Air, have pledged to lease around 199 additional aircraft worth an estimated USD 12-16 billion through their respective leasing entities in Gujarat’s GIFT City, a move that will almost triple the number of commercial aircraft currently leased through the international financial services centre (IFSC).

title: Aditya Birla Group entity seeks GIFT City nod to enter aircraft leasing
